counterfactual.change: Reduced dt from 0.02374 to 0.001 with all else identical (same 2 steps); this avoids the fast-body substep path (~42 substeps/step) and energy stays conserved, so no violation.

explanation: Free-fall with controller disabled, no walls and no contacts, yet energy grows ~140 J per step. Position update uses correct dt (dx = vx*dt matches), but velocity gain is ~1.397 m/s per 0.0237 s step vs expected g*dt=0.233 m/s (~6x gravity). The steps report 42-43 substeps_in_step triggered by the fast body (~52 m/s). Likely cause: gravity velocity update is over-applied when the fast-path substep splitting is active (scaled by substep count factor instead of dt/substeps), pumping kinetic energy each step while controller_work stays 0, so energy_bound is exceeded by step 2. Small dt removes the failure.
vision_note: The upper body moves rapidly down and to the right across steps 0 to 2 while the lower-left body stays nearly stationary. No walls, contacts, waypoints or driven-body motion are visible to justify a large energy gain.
